title: Salt Cod Fritters
subtitle: Portuguese bacalhau fritters with potato
excerpt: Portugal's beloved bacalhau cakes: salt cod desalted over two days, flaked and mixed with mashed potato, egg, and herbs, formed into small cakes, and pan-fried until crisp and golden outside and soft within. A staple of the Portuguese table.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pastéis de bacalhau (salt cod cakes) are one of the most widely eaten dishes in Portugal and its diaspora, where they appear at every occasion from casual weekday dinners to celebration meals. Portugal's relationship with salt cod (bacalhau) goes back to the fifteenth century, when Portuguese fishermen began catching cod off Newfoundland and preserving it in salt for the voyage home. The Portuguese consume more salt cod per capita than any other country; there are said to be 365 recipes for bacalhau, one for every day of the year. The fritters are the most accessible for a home cook. The cod must be desalted by soaking in cold water in the fridge, changing the water several times over 24 to 48 hours; the time depends on the thickness of the fish.

content.text: Desalting the cod properly is the most important step: taste a small piece before using; it should be pleasantly salty, not aggressively so. If still very salty after 48 hours, soak for another 12 hours. The mixture should hold together without additional flour; if it is too wet, refrigerate it for 30 minutes before forming the cakes.

items.preparation: desalted: soaked in cold water in the fridge for 24 to 48 hours, changing water 3 times; skin and bones removed; flaked
peeled, boiled, and mashed; left to cool

content.text: Simmer the desalted cod in unsalted water for 8 minutes until it flakes easily. Drain and cool. Remove any remaining skin or bones and flake finely. Cook the onion in a little oil for 5 minutes until soft.

Combine the flaked cod, mashed potato, cooked onion, garlic, parsley, and eggs. Season with pepper; taste before adding any salt as the cod will still be salty. Mix until combined. The mixture should be firm enough to hold its shape. Refrigerate for 20 minutes if soft.

With wet hands, form the mixture into oval cakes about 5 cm long and 1.5 cm thick. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the cakes in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper. Serve warm with lemon wedges and aioli or Portuguese hot sauce.
